q-50100.name: Question 1
q-50100.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/778cc96e20eead41160c37b8a39373d789c166a9d516a70591f7ba7b315f3fbf.png)

Which expression represents the total finite area enclosed between the curves $y={x}^{4}-{x}^{2}$ and $y={x}^{3}-x,$ as shown above?

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*
q-50100.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=y={x}^{4}-{x}^{2}$ and $g(x)={x}^{3}-x.$ First, we find the intersections of the two curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ {x}^{4}-{x}^{2} & ={x}^{3}-x \\ {x}^{2}({x}^{2}-1) & =x({x}^{2}-1) \\ ({x}^{2}-x)({x}^{2}-1) & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}-x)(x+1)(x-1) & =0 \\ x(x-1)(x+1)(x-1) & =0 \\ x & =-1,0,1\end{aligned}
$$

The area we want consists of two regions: ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/d84bd9bccba15a91ab54ee0dc64fb344c191384a14ee5d5c2fb857dc18fc63db.png)

We have:

- For the area ${A}_{1},$ we have $x\in [-1,0],$ and the upper function is $g(x)$ while the lower function is $f(x).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[g(x)-f(x)]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[({x}^{3}-x)-({x}^{4}-{x}^{2})]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(-{x}^{4}+{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the area ${A}_{2},$ we have $x\in [0,1],$ and the upper function is $f(x)$ while the lower function is $g(x).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[f(x)-g(x)]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[({x}^{4}-{x}^{2})-({x}^{3}-x)]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(-{x}^{4}+{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-50100.html:
Question 1
?

Which expression represents the total finite area enclosed between the curves y=x4−x2 and y=x3−x, as shown above?

(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)

a
∫01(−x4+x3)dx+∫01(−x2+x)dx
b
∫−11(−x4−x)dx
c
∫−10(−x4+x3+x2−x)dx+∫01(x4−x3−x2+x)dx
d
∫−11(x3−x4)dx
e
∫−10(x2−x)dx+∫−10(x4−x3)dx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let f(x)=y=x4−x2 and g(x)=x3−x. First, we find the intersections of the two curves: f(x)=g(x)x4−x2=x3−xx2(x2−1)=x(x2−1)(x2−x)(x2−1)=0(x2−x)(x+1)(x−1)=0x(x−1)(x+1)(x−1)=0x=−1,0,1

The area we want consists of two regions: A1 and A2.

We have:

  • For the area A1, we have x∈[−1,0], and the upper function is g(x) while the lower function is f(x). So, the area is given by A1=∫−10[g(x)−f(x)]dx=∫−10[(x3−x)−(x4−x2)]dx=∫−10(−x4+x3+x2−x)dx.
  • For the area A2, we have x∈[0,1], and the upper function is f(x) while the lower function is g(x). So, the area is given by A2=∫01[f(x)−g(x)]dx=∫01[(x4−x2)−(x3−x)]dx=∫01(x4−x3−x2+x)dx.

Therefore, the required area is given by A=A1+A2=∫−10(−x4+x3+x2−x)dx+∫01(x4−x3−x2+x)dx.

q-83553.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/dbb0eea61f7b4a4c6aa9f9b06462c327c9c6a366b5ff0ca21378f9be888f5ede.png)

What is the total finite area enclosed between the curves $x=f(y)=3{y}^{3}+6{y}^{2}$ and $x=g(y)=3y+6,$ as shown above?  

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*
q-83553.worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the two curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 3{y}^{3}+6{y}^{2} & =3y+6 \\ {y}^{3}+2{y}^{2} & =y+2 \\ {y}^{2}(y+2)-(y+2) & =0 \\ ({y}^{2}-1)(y+2) & =0 \\ (y+2)(y-1)(y+1) & =0 \\ y & =-2,-1,1.\end{aligned}
$$

The area we want consists of two regions: ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/aa11be3a96d2055899bd17d700f1e59e7715bae2550d60d5c3a05d9f999b4008.png)

 

- For the area ${A}_{1},$ we have $y\in [-2,-1],$ and the right function is $f(y)$ while the left function is $g(y).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}[f(y)-g(y)]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}(3{y}^{3}+6{y}^{2}-3y-6)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={(\frac{3{y}^{4}}{4}+2{y}^{3}-\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}-6y)|}_{-2}^{-1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{4}-2-\frac{3}{2}+6)-(12-16-6+12) \\  & =\frac{13}{4}-2 \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the area ${A}_{2},$ we have $y\in [-1,1],$ and the right function is $g(y)$ while the left function is $f(y).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(g(y)-f(y))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(3y+6-3{y}^{3}-6{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={(\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}+6y-\frac{3{y}^{4}}{4}-2{y}^{3})|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2}+6-\frac{3}{4}-2)-(\frac{3}{2}-6-\frac{3}{4}+2) \\  & =(4+\frac{3}{4})-(\frac{3}{4}-4) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=\frac{5}{4}+8=\frac{37}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/2cd4f059ef78b3ce7d6043dc216494340c08eb43edeab9b3869cd733c2f6d144.png)

Find the total finite area $A$ enclosed between the curves $y=f(x)={x}^{3}-13x-10$ and $y=2,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*

$A=$

{{field-1}}
q-351774.worked_solution:
Let $g(x)=2.$ First, we find the intersections of the two curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ {x}^{3}-13x-10 & =2 \\ {x}^{3}-13x-12 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $x=-1$ is a root of ${x}^{3}-13x-12,$ and if we divide ${x}^{3}-13x-12$ by $x+1$ using synthetic division, we get ${x}^{2}-x-12.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)({x}^{2}-x-12) & =0 \\ (x+1)(x-4)(x+3) & =0 \\ x & =-3,-1,4.\end{aligned}
$$

The area we want consists of two regions: ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/3c4181d72f44f0190d03fa4239718e4f2877fda19a7b1f87421ef2746e27bcbc.png)

  

- For the area ${A}_{1},$ we have $x\in [-3,-1],$ and the upper function is $f(x)$ while the lower function is $g(x).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}(f(x)-g(x))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}(({x}^{3}-13x-10)-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}({x}^{3}-13x-12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}{x}^{2}-12x){|}_{-3}^{-1} \\  & =(\frac{(-1)^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}(-1)^{2}-12(-1))-(\frac{(-3)^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}(-3)^{2}-12(-3)) \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{13}{2}+12)-(\frac{81}{4}-\frac{117}{2}+36) \\  & =\frac{23}{4}-(-\frac{9}{4}) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the area ${A}_{2},$ we have $x\in [-1,4],$ and the upper function is $g(x)$ while the lower function is $f(x).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{-1}^{4}(g(x)-f(x))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{4}(2-({x}^{3}-13x-10))\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{4}({x}^{3}-13x-12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}{x}^{2}-12x){|}_{-1}^{4} \\  & =-(\frac{{4}^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}({4}^{2})-12(4))+(\frac{(-1)^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}(-1)^{2}-12(-1)) \\  & =-(64-104-48)+(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{13}{2}+12) \\  & =-(-88)+(\frac{23}{4}) \\  & =\frac{375}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=8+\frac{375}{4}=\frac{407}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the total finite area $A$ enclosed between the curves $x=-2{y}^{1/3}$ and $x=-\frac{y}{8},$ as shown above? Do not round the answer.

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*

$A=$

{{field-1}}
q-351822.worked_solution:
Let $f(y)=-2{y}^{1/3}$ and $g(y)=-\frac{y}{8}.$ First, we find the intersections of the two curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ -2{y}^{1/3} & =-\frac{y}{8} \\ 16{y}^{1/3} & =y \\ 4096y & ={y}^{3} \\ y({y}^{2}-4096) & =0 \\ y(y-64)(y+64) & =0 \\ y & =0,\pm 64\end{aligned}
$$

The area we want consists of two regions: ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/ce1c5d7fe654b406671eebf60eb65af5e11e20bb83adc08d81f6afca14856228.png)

 

- For the area ${A}_{1},$ we have $y\in [-64,0],$ and the right function is $f(y)$ while the left function is $g(y).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{-64}^{0}(f(y)-g(y))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-64}^{0}(-2{y}^{1/3}-(-\frac{y}{8}))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-64}^{0}(-2{y}^{1/3}+\frac{y}{8})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={(-\frac{3{y}^{4/3}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{16})|}_{-64}^{0} \\  & =0-(-384+256) \\  & =128.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the area ${A}_{2},$ we have $y\in [0,64],$ and the right function is $g(y)$ while the left function is $f(y).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{0}^{64}(g(y)-f(y))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{64}(-\frac{y}{8}-(-2{y}^{1/3}))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{64}(-\frac{y}{8}+2{y}^{1/3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={(-\frac{{y}^{2}}{16}+\frac{3{y}^{4/3}}{2})|}_{0}^{64} \\  & =(-256+384)-0 \\  & =128.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=128+128=256.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the total finite area $A$ enclosed between the curves $y=15{x}^{4}+1$ and $y=15{x}^{2}+1,$ as shown above.  Do not round the answer.

$A=$

{{field-1}}
q-353285.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=15{x}^{4}+1$ and $g(x)=15{x}^{2}+1.$ First, we find the intersections of the curves:

$$
\begin{aligned} & f(x)=g(x) \\  & 15{x}^{4}+1=15{x}^{2}+1 \\  & 15{x}^{4}=15{x}^{2} \\  & 15{x}^{4}-15{x}^{2}=0 \\  & 15{x}^{2}({x}^{2}-1)=0 \\ x & =-1,0,1\end{aligned}
$$

The area we want consists of two regions: ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/66ae463184e8d5fc9f667019be7fc5c893aea736a6d0dad8fa6a2619df9f08e8.png)

- For the area ${A}_{1},$ we have $x\in [-1,0],$ and the upper function is $g(x)$ while the lower function is $f(x).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(g(x)-f(x))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}((15{x}^{2}+1)-(15{x}^{4}+1))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(15{x}^{2}-15{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(5{x}^{3}-3{x}^{5})|}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =0-(5(-1)^{3}-3(-1)^{5}) \\  & =0-(-5+3) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the area ${A}_{2},$ we have $x\in [0,1],$ and the upper function is $g(x)$ while the lower function is $f(x).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(g(x)-f(x))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}((15{x}^{2}+1)-(15{x}^{4}+1))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(15{x}^{2}-15{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(5{x}^{3}-3{x}^{5})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(5-3)-0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=2+2=4.\end{aligned}
$$
